questions.questionText: When does an object falling vertically through the air reach terminal velocity?

options.text: when the acceleration of the object becomes negative
when the acceleration of the object is equal to g
when the air resistance equals the weight of the object
when the air resistance is greater than the weight of the object

questions.questionText:
An object always has mass but does not always have weight.
What must be present and acting on the mass for it to have weight?

options.text: a gravitational field
a set of scales
displaced water
friction due to air resistance

questions.questionText:
A force acting on a moving ball causes its motion to change. This force stays constant.
What makes the force produce a greater change in the motion of the ball?

options.text: decreasing the total mass of the ball
increasing the temperature of the ball
using a ball with a hollow centre but the same mass
using a different material for the ball so that it has a lower density but the same mass

questions.questionText:
A car is moving in a straight line on a level road. Its engine provides a forward force on the car. A
second force of equal size acts on the car due to resistive forces.
Which statement describes what happens?

options.text: The car changes direction.
The car moves at a constant speed.
The car slows down.
The car speeds up.

questions.questionText: Which expression gives the momentum of an object?

options.text: mass × acceleration
mass × gravitational field strength
mass × velocity
1 × mass × (velocity)2

questions.questionText:
As energy is transferred into different forms, it eventually becomes dissipated.
What does this mean?

options.text: All the energy disappears.
The energy finally changes into every possible form of energy.
The energy spreads out among the objects and their surroundings.
The total amount of energy becomes less.

questions.questionText:
When molecules of a gas rebound from a wall of a container, the wall experiences a pressure.
What is the cause of this pressure?

options.text: the change in energy of the molecules
the change in momentum of the molecules
the change in power of the molecules
the change in speed of the molecules

questions.questionText:
On a cold day, a metal front-door knob X and a similar plastic knob Y are at the same
temperature.
Why does X feel cooler to the touch than Y?

options.text: X convects thermal energy better than Y.
X is a better thermal conductor than Y.
X is a better insulator than Y.
X is a better radiator of thermal energy than Y.

questions.questionText:

In the glass, the wavelength of the light is 4.0 × 10–7m.
What is the frequency of the light?

options.text: 80Hz

20Hz–150kHz

150Hz–20kHz

Which method is used to demagnetise the magnet?

questions.questionText:
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a rechargeable battery is 6.0V.
What does this mean?

options.text: 6.0J is the maximum energy the battery can provide in 1.0s.
6.0J is the total energy the battery can provide before it has to be recharged.
6.0J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a charge of 1.0C around a complete circuit.
6.0J of energy is provided by the battery to drive a current of 1.0A around a complete circuit.

questions.questionText:
A student measures the potential difference across a device and the current in the device.
Which calculation gives the resistance of the device?

options.text: current + potential difference
current ÷ potential difference
potential difference ÷ current
potential difference × current

questions.questionText:
A student sets up this circuit.
What is the purpose of the circuit?

options.text: to allow a lamp to be made dimmer or brighter as required
to amplify the sound of a voice
to light a lamp in the dark
to sound a bell when the temperature rises

questions.questionText: Which statement about electromagnetic induction is correct?

options.text: A strong magnet that is held stationary near a stationary conductor causes a greater effect than a weak magnet.
The effect occurs when a magnet and a conductor are both moved with the same speed and in the same direction.
The effect occurs when a magnet is moved away from a nearby conductor.
The effect only occurs when a magnet is moved towards a conductor.

questions.questionText:
Power losses in transmission cables are reduced by increasing the transmission voltage.
What is the explanation for this reduction?

options.text: The current decreases, reducing thermal energy losses.
The current increases, increasing the flow of charge.
The resistance of the cable increases, reducing the current.
The resistance of the cable decreases.
